lead.en: Nana (BTS E3, opened 1999) is the name for a stretch of lower Sukhumvit between roughly Soi 1 and Soi 9 whose odd and even sides 'are like two different worlds': to the north, Soi Nana (Soi 4) carries the bar strip and the three-floor Nana Plaza complex of about two dozen go-go bars, while Soi 3/3/1 - 'Soi Arab' - has anchored a Middle Eastern community of restaurants and shisha cafes since Shahrazad opened in 1983. Daytime it reads as a business-and-hotel lane; the same blocks run late. Daily-life support is unusually strong for a nightlife district: a 24-hour supermarket block at Soi 5 (snippet-level), Villa Market walking distance, and Bumrungrad hospital 350-500 m up Soi 3 with its own shuttle. Rents in the surrounding subdistrict average 37,429 THB for 1-bed and 60,855 THB for 2-bed asking, bracketing the app's 28,000/60,000 estimate. What the unit lacks is quiet and green: the nearest big parks - Benchasiri at Phrom Phong and Lumphini across Rama IV - sit outside the clipped catchment, and only 1.4 ha of park is mapped inside.

strengths.en: Transit centrality: E3 on the Sukhumvit Line, described as one of the busiest BTS stations, with three exits covering the Soi 3 (Arab quarter + pier), Soi 4 (bar strip) and south-side frontage
Two distinct food communities within 300 m of the exits: the Soi 3/1 Arab quarter (Yemeni, Egyptian, Lebanese kitchens since 1983-86) and the Sukhumvit frontage's tourist-and-hotel dining
Healthcare at the doorstep: Bumrungrad at 33 Soi Nana Nuea with a free shuttle from BTS Nana - a rare in-catchment amenity
Consistent rent reality: independent portal data brackets the app's 28,000/60,000 asking estimate, with ordinary 1-bed stock found at 27,000 THB ~400 m from the station

tradeoffs.en: Nightlife is the load-bearing feature and the main cost: noise 'until very late' near Soi 4 (and Soi 11, though that block sits on the st.asok side of the clip)
A scam/tout environment is repeatedly reported around the plaza and Soi 4 frontage - padded bills, touts, spiking warnings - even though the same sources call it 'generally safe' beyond that

Green inside the clipped unit is minimal: 1.4 ha mapped on 0.97 sq km, with Benchasiri outside at Phrom Phong and Lumphini's nearest edge a ~0.7-0.8 km boundary case requiring an arterial-road crossing
Space-per-baht is poor: 'you often pay more for less space than further-out Bangkok neighborhoods', and Sukhumvit traffic is heavy for car users

variation.en: Odd/even split: Soi 3/3/1 Arab community quarter vs Soi 4/5 hotel-bar strip - 'like two completely different worlds'
Soi-by-soi noise gradient: frontage and Soi 4 loud until late; deeper residential pockets 'quieter by day'; guide names Soi 10/12 as quieter but that sits beyond the east clip

West/east clip asymmetry: the Soi 9-13 hotel cluster (Marriott, Hyatt Regency Sukhumvit, Sofitel/Ramada) falls outside or borderline into st.asok's catchment, though station guides list it under Nana exits
South-of-Sukhumvit even-soi blocks are the residential face, with their far southern depth clipped off by st.lumphini's catchment

fit.en: Good fit: long-stay expats and remote workers who want centrality, transit, food diversity and hospital access and can accept noise - 'single professionals, couples, and even families who want central access' per the residential guide
Poor fit: light sleepers or families prioritizing green and quiet - the nearest major parks are outside the clipped unit
Poor fit: budget renters wanting space and car-dependent residents - higher cost per sqm and heavy Sukhumvit traffic
Poor fit (situational): first-time tourists averse to touts and bill-padding around the plaza; the same area is rated 'generally safe' for alert residents

uncertainties: The mapped 1.4 ha park could not be identified (Overpass/Nominatim failed) - green 10's basis is unresolved and probably rests on station-area proximity to parks outside the clip [nana-c14]
Clip geometry rests on Wikipedia infobox coordinates with a suspected error for BTS Asok; east/west clip soi boundaries carry ~1-2-soi uncertainty until GIS-verified [nana-c15]

Scam specifics (padded-bill incidents, 2026 bar-fine levels) are snippet-level because TripAdvisor and Reddit fetches returned 403; only the general tout/price environment is body-read supported [nana-c12]
Bar count (24 vs 30) and closing hour (02:00 vs 03:00) conflict between the operator's site and Wikipedia [nana-c04]
High-season tourist surges and weekday/weekend rhythm differences: not found in body-read sources [Q05]
Nana Plaza's district attribution ('Khlong Toei' per Wikipedia) conflicts with the app's Watthana-majority split for Soi 4 [nana-c18]
